catalog_quote: Since contrasts in stress placement occurs in minimal environments ..., stress placement is recognized as significant. It might be concluded that since stress occurs on any of the last four syllables of stress groups a four-way contrast in stress placement exists, necessitating the recognition of four stress-group types. It seems significant, however, that only a two-way stress contrast exists in minimal environments (e.g., qitulud 'will push', qitulud 'will accorripany'; qumali 'will come', qumeli 'will call'; qidew 'omen bird', qidew 'a variety of snake'.) and that a three- or four-way stress contrast is not found in anything approaching minimal environments. ... sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: TOZ Offsite Storage L.SOC.95.53.1.05 (33) (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.quote: The grammar sketch never uses the words 'stress' or 'accent' (grep: zero hits). Its only prosodic statement: 'When verb stems of the cvcv pattern are inflected by suffixes -an or -on, the vowel length shifts to the second vowel.' This repeats the 1993 phonology sketch's length-shift-under-suffixation already recorded in the record's morphology_note; word prosody is treated as lexically specified vowel length, consistent with a lexical two-way contrast.
sources.note: Would let a reader verify that Newell's 1970 stress minimal pairs (gayang 'hawk'/'spear', qidew, qitulud) are entered in 1993 as length pairs, pinning the 1970-stress = 1993-length equivalence the record asserts; low priority because it cannot change the LEXICAL coding.

sources.quote: Dialect-identification front matter only (Batad valley, north-central Ifugao; a few thousand speakers; ISBN 971-1059-24-X); nothing on stress. Useful only as identity confirmation that the 1970 and 1993 sources describe the same Batad valley lect.
